questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It guarantees they will yield to you.
It does not mean they see you.
It is not worth the effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to make sure a driver will yield to you. A driver may look at you but still not notice you.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, release the brake. If the rear brake locks on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view of the road behind you. They make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice using your convex mirrors before you ride.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in groups communicate. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: Since motorcycles are hard to see at night, what should a rider do?

options.text: Stay directly in front of another vehicle's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed. Also increase your following distance, use the headlights of other vehicles to see ahead, use your high beam (unless another vehicle is near), and be ready to change your position in the lane.

questions.question: When turning on a three-wheeled motorcycle, what is best to do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles turn differently than two-wheeled ones. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of a curve and then straighten out your path.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Push the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walk, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pushing the grip in your desired direction makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Use only two fingers to grab the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: To brake safely, use all four fingers to squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly. Increase the force gradually.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It applies some rear braking when the front brake is used.
It applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
It applies equal braking to both wheels at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Signs that show rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns or stops. When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it down, it means they plan to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: If the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left portion of a lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of each lane. When the road is wet, this oily strip becomes slippery and unsafe. Ride to the side of the center strip while still staying in your lane.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and moving slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge how far away they are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: When looking through a turn to see where you are going, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The group will pull off at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points one finger up, it tells the group to form a single line.

questions.question: When you are being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This prevents the other driver from coming back into your lane too early.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: First apply the front brake, then the rear.
First apply the rear brake, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should travel in a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Two-wheeled motorcycles can ride in a staggered formation, but three-wheeled motorcycles are too wide. Riders on three-wheeled motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have used the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Should be avoided because it causes heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if it is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from injury and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan your route based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: At intersections, be extra careful. Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: The best protection when riding is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best protection against crashes is to stay away from other vehicles. Leave plenty of space so you have time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Wearing proper safety gear is also important.
